subject: sea robin fish
title: This Fish Walks on Six Legs, and the Legs Can Taste

scenes.text: This fish walks on the seafloor. And its legs do something no leg should.
The northern sea robin, found from Nova Scotia to Florida. Three leg-like spines on each side, split off from its fins.
In a tank, scientists buried mussels under sand. The sea robins walked straight to them and dug them up.
They even found capsules of ground mussel with no visible clue. The legs are coated in tiny bumps packed with taste receptors.
A close cousin has smooth, rod-shaped legs. It walked over the buried food and never noticed.
Other fish follow the sea robin around to steal what it digs up. Legs that taste, and a crowd that knows it.

description:
The northern sea robin walks across the seabed on six leg-like spines, and research published in Current Biology in 2024 showed those legs are covered in papillae packed with taste receptors.
In lab tests the fish found mussels buried under sand and even capsules of ground mussel with no visual clue. A related species with smooth, rod-shaped legs could not find the hidden food. Other fish follow sea robins to take what they dig up.
What other animal has a body part doing the wrong job? Comment below.
first_comment: There are about 125 sea robin species worldwide, and only some of them have the tasting legs. Which animal with a strange sense should we cover next?
